name: Gatsby
tagline: The React-based static site generator built around GraphQL

seo.title: Gatsby: Overview, Strengths, and Trade-offs in 2026
seo.description: What Gatsby is today, why its GraphQL data layer was influential, and what to consider before starting a new project on it.

intro:
Gatsby popularized the idea of a React static site generator with a normalized GraphQL data layer: plugins pulled content from anywhere, unified it into one schema, and pages queried that schema at build time. For a period it was the default choice for React developers who wanted a content site, and its plugin ecosystem was the main reason people picked it.

Its trajectory since then is the honest part of the story. Maintenance pace slowed, the GraphQL layer became a source of friction as projects grew, and frameworks that compile away the client runtime took over the content-site niche. Gatsby still runs existing sites fine, and its incremental build story is real. For a new build in 2026, most teams are weighing it against far more active alternatives. This is a reference entry used by the comparison and migration pages.
